analysis.investment_thesis: Nanta Tech fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions — a 3.4% earnings yield (1/29.6 P/E) is far below the 12% threshold, and a 0.47% ROE implies ROIC nowhere near the 20%+ bar. Cheap AND good? It is neither.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 57.36% signals skin in the game
Exposure to AV integration/service robots — a growing niche
Debt-light micro-cap with optionality if execution improves
key_risks: ROE of 0.47% indicates capital is earning nothing — antithesis of Magic Formula
P/E of 29.60 on negligible earnings = earnings yield ~3.4%, deeply overvalued
Incorporated 2023 — no 3-year track record of sustained ROIC
red_flags: Zero operating history (founded 2023) to validate any metric
Market cap of INR 139 Cr on microscopic profits suggests speculative pricing
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula is mechanical: rank on earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital (EBIT/invested capital). Nanta Tech flunks both. A P/E of 29.60 corresponds to an earnings yield of ~3.4%, less than a risk-free G-Sec, and ROE of 0.47% tells me invested capital is producing essentially no EBIT. A company cannot be "cheap" at 30x earnings when those earnings are a rounding error, and it cannot be "good" when capital returns are sub-1%. This is the bottom decile on both axes — the exact opposite of what the formula seeks.

Incorporated in 2023, there is no multi-year ROIC record to verify, no evidence of durable economics in AV integration or service robots, and the float is thin with 57% promoter concentration. Even granting the thematic appeal of robotics/AV, the systematic screen says pass. I would not include this in a Magic Formula portfolio, and a discretionary override is unwarranted given the absence of data.
